description: Estimate what a job will cost in credits BEFORE submitting it, and whether the connected account can afford it right now. Spends nothing. Pass the job (generate_music, generate_sound, generate_loop, cover_stem, edit_lyrics, fill_gap, render_midi, train_instrument, cover_song, separate_stems, split_soundtrack, transcribe, audio_to_session, convert_project, bounce_session, spot_video, score_to_picture, sound_design, reframe_video, analyze_song, detect_chords, beat_grid, identify_sound, supervise_cues, analyze_midi, render_score, mix, mix_preset, session_from_stems, check_take) and the same args you would give the job tool (duration_seconds, models, instruments; for render_midi: notes + bpm / tempo_map or duration_seconds, voice_split / voices, takes — takes are free, voices cost one batch per ~6; for render_score: parts + bpm / tempo_map — planned exactly as the job plans it (lines, player rows, length), and `refused` says when the job would refuse it; render_score {generator} is priced as the generator will PLAY it — the band asks the generator for its piece (free) and its parts are priced, a film arc's bare seat at the section it plays (plan.part_rows: each part's rows)). `account.remaining` is the largest ONE charge the account can pay now: an active first-score grant pays a job it has the credits left for, else the tightest of the hour, the day and the month. The estimate follows the planes' own price table; the gate is authoritative and a refusal names the exact price.

args.description: The arguments you intend to pass to the job tool; only the price-relevant ones matter.

job.description: Which job to price (a doseedo_ tool name or recipe verb is accepted too).

name: doseedo_quote
title: Price a job
